metadata.question: Were the water levels in Lake Kariba in December, 2019 higher than the water levels seen in December, 2018?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about water levels in Lake Kariba in December 2018 vs December 2019. This requires comparing water extent/levels between two time periods. For water detection, I should use: 1. Sentinel-1 SAR data - good for water detection as it's not affected by clouds 2. JRC Global Surface Water dataset - specifically designed for water detection 3. MODIS or Landsat with water indices The JRC dataset would be most reliable for this purpose. I'll use the JRC Global Surface Water dataset which provides monthly water occurrence data. Steps: 1. Define Lake Kariba geometry 2. Get JRC Monthly Water History for December 2018 and December 2019 3. Calculate water extent for both periods 4. Compare and determine if 2019 had higher water levels I need to handle: - Checking if data exists for both periods (C1) - Validating pixel counts (C2) - Ensuring calculations are valid (C3) The JRC dataset has monthly water classification from 1984-2020, so it should cover both 2018 and 2019. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const lakeKariba = ee.Geometry.Polygon([ [26.8, -17.0], [28.5, -17.0], [28.5, -16.0], [26.8, -16.0], [26.8, -17.0] ]); // 2. Data Acquisition - JRC Global Surface Water Monthly History const dec2018 = ee.ImageCollection('JRC/GSW1_3/MonthlyHistory') .filterDate('2018-12-01', '2019-01-01') .filterBounds(lakeKariba); const dec2019 = ee.ImageCollection('JRC/GSW1_3/MonthlyHistory') .filterDate('2019-12-01', '2020-01-01') .filterBounds(lakeKariba); // Check collection sizes const count2018 = dec2018.size().getInfo(); const count2019 = dec2019.size().getInfo(); console.log(`2018 Images: ${count2018}, 2019 Images: ${count2019}`); if (count2018 === 0 || count2019 === 0) { console.log("C1"); return; } // Get first image from each collection const img2018 = dec2018.first(); const img2019 = dec2019.first(); // Calculate water area for each period // Water classification: 2 = water, 3 = not water const water2018 = img2018.eq(2); const water2019 = img2019.eq(2); // Calculate pixel counts and area const stats2018 = water2018.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry: lakeKariba, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }); const stats2019 = water2019.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry: lakeKariba, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }); const waterPixels2018 = stats2018.get('water').getInfo(); const waterPixels2019 = stats2019.get('water').getInfo(); console.log(`2018 Water Pixels: ${waterPixels2018}`); console.log(`2019 Water Pixels: ${waterPixels2019}`); // Check for valid pixels if (waterPixels2018 === 0 || waterPixels2019 === 0) { console.log("C2"); return; } // Check for calculation failures if (waterPixels2018 === null || waterPixels2019 === null || isNaN(waterPixels2018) || isNaN(waterPixels2019)) { console.log("C3"); return; } // Compare water levels (higher pixel count = higher water level) const waterHigher2019 = waterPixels2019 > waterPixels2018; console.log(`Water Change: ${((waterPixels2019 - waterPixels2018) / waterPixels2018 * 100).toFixed(1)}%`); if (waterHigher2019) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
